comments.author: rnimje-nasuni
comments.body: If the connection is broken, _engine.dispose() this line itself can fail. Can we do like forgetting the connection first, then try to clean it up? If cleanup fails, log a warning and move on.

comments.author: avinash-b-nasuni
comments.body: Refactored [dispose_root_engine](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) to reset [_engine = None](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) before calling [dispose()](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html). This way, even if [dispose()](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) raises on a broken connection, the singleton is already cleared and the next [get_root_engine()](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) call will create a fresh engine. Added a try/except that logs a warning with traceback if [dispose()](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Visual%20Studio%20Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) itself fails.

comments.author: Copilot
comments.body: The warning message says "pool has been reset", but if `engine_to_dispose.dispose()` raises, the pool/engine may not have been disposed—only the cached singleton was cleared. Consider rewording the log to reflect what's guaranteed (e.g., cache cleared / new engine will be created on next use) to avoid misleading operational logs.

comments.author: sasi-nasuni
comments.body:
We are disposing the engine on every exception, is that okay ?(Assuming a non connection related exception occurred which would still leave the pool connection healthy and in that case we would clearing out healthy connection to create a new one). 
(On another thought since it is a single connection, it would not matter even if we get one more by killing the current one)

comments.author: avinash-b-nasuni
comments.body: Good catch! With NullPool there's no pool of healthy connections to lose, so disposing on any exception is harmless and keeps the logic simple.
